The proposals aim to balance ease of investing with investor protection by implementing safeguards like KYC checks and electronic fund trails. Sebi seeks public comments on these changes until June 10th.

articles.title: NEET paper leak row: Congress demands resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leaders demanded the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan, the Union Education Minister, over the NEET-UG paper leak scandal.  They accused the government of a "money-making racket" involving people linked to the ruling establishment and claimed that the incident had caused immense trauma for 22 lakh students. Rahul Gandhi called for the Prime Minister's intervention, while Mallikarjun Kharge, the Congress president, alleged that the Modi government was undermining student credibility through repeated paper leaks.  Jairam Ramesh, a Congress general secretary, criticized the government's lack of action and incompetence in addressing exam reforms.

articles.title: Colorado governor faces backlash over clemency for 2020 election denier Tina Peters
articles.rephrased_article: Governor Jared Polis of Colorado faced criticism from fellow Democrats and some Republicans after commuting the prison sentence of former county clerk Tina Peters, a 2020 election denier convicted of tampering with election equipment.  Secretary of State Jena Griswold called the decision "an affront to our democracy", while President Donald Trump praised Peters' release on social media. Peters expressed remorse for her actions, but Governor Polis defended his commutation by arguing that her sentence was disproportionate for a first-time offender.

articles.title: Zimbabwe’s diaspora reshapes real estate and farming investment trends | Features | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Zimbabwean digital influencers, Kundai Chitima and Kelvin Birioti, are influencing diaspora investment decisions through their social media content.  Their videos highlight opportunities in real estate, farming, and market trends, prompting some diaspora members to reconsider returning or investing in Zimbabwe. Nyashadzashe Nguwo, an Africa market entry advisor based in the UK, states that many individuals are relocating due to a combination of emotional and lifestyle-driven factors, including a desire to reconnect with their roots and contribute to national development.  Catherine Mutisi, a diaspora member who had previously invested in Zimbabwe, credits social media content for shifting her perspective on returning permanently. Economic pressures, such as high unemployment rates and rising living costs, continue to influence migration decisions, but the strong economic link between Zimbabwe and its diaspora remains significant, with diaspora investment playing a crucial role in various sectors.

articles.title: Andalucíans to vote in election seen as gauge of Spain’s wider political change | Spain | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming election in Andalucía, Spain's most populous region, is expected to deliver an absolute majority for the conservative People’s Party (PP) and further weaken the Socialists. Juan Manuel Moreno Bonilla, the PP regional president, seeks to capitalize on scandals surrounding Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and his administration.  The PP aims to portray the election as a referendum on Sánchez's leadership, while Vox is expected to gain seats. The outcome will have implications for Spain's upcoming general election next year.

articles.title: T.N. Cabinet portfolios: CM Vijay to hold Home; Finance for Sengottaiyan; Aadhav Arjuna gets PWD - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, has announced the portfolios for his cabinet members. Vijay will oversee key departments including Home, Police, and IAS/IPS officers.  N. Anand, the deputy chief minister, will handle Rural Development and Water Resources. Other ministers have been assigned specific responsibilities in areas such as health, education, finance, and energy. The Governor has approved the recommendations.

articles.title: Arrest of Iraqi terror suspect with alleged links to Iran’s Quds Force is astonishing but not surprising | Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: An alleged Iraqi commander of an Iranian-backed militia group, Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, has been arrested in the US on charges of orchestrating 18 terrorist attacks across Europe and Canada since the beginning of the Iran war. The complaint alleges that al-Saadi is responsible for a string of recent firebombings, an arson attack on a synagogue, and a shooting at the US consulate in Toronto, as well as a wave of attacks on Jewish targets in the UK.  Al-Saadi allegedly posted claims of responsibility for attacks on social media platforms under the name of Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamia (HAYI), a group believed to be linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). The arrest comes as no surprise to investigators and analysts who have long suspected Iranian involvement in these attacks.

articles.title: Palestinian leaders hold rare party meeting as polls show rising discontent
articles.rephrased_article: Mahmoud Abbas, the 90-year-old Palestinian President, was re-elected as head of Fatah at its first major conference in a decade.  The meeting comes amid rising discontent among Palestinians, with polls indicating widespread dissatisfaction and calls for Abbas' resignation. The conference aims to address these concerns and implement reforms, but critics point out internal divisions and nepotism within the party.  Despite promises of elections and unity, many Palestinians feel that Fatah has lost its way and is prioritizing its own interests over those of the Palestinian people.

articles.title: Where did Eurovision go wrong? | Music News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Eurovision Song Contest, a major global entertainment event, is facing controversy due to Israel's participation.  Israel’s President Isaac Herzog, and the Israeli Broadcasting Authority (Kan) have spent significant resources promoting Israel's presence in the contest, while artists and broadcasters are boycotting it. Critics argue that Israel's actions in Gaza constitute a genocide and question the event's ability to remain apolitical.  The EBU has defended its decision, citing Kan's independence from the Israeli government, but critics point out a perceived double standard compared to Russia's ban following its invasion of Ukraine. The controversy has led to boycotts by broadcasters in several countries, including the Netherlands, Slovenia, Spain, Iceland, and Ireland, while artists like Molly Nilsson have called for a boycott until Israel is removed.  The financial impact of these boycotts is significant, with some estimates suggesting that it could remove millions of euros from the contest's funding pool.

articles.title: NIA chargesheets ‘mastermind,’ four others in Cambodia-linked ‘cyber slavery’ case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) filed a charge sheet against five individuals, including absconding mastermind Anand Kumar Singh, in a case of human trafficking and “cyber slavery” in Cambodia. Three accused, Abhay Nath Dubey, Rohit Yadav, and Abhiranjan Kumar, were arrested upon arrival in Delhi from Cambodia in February. The syndicate lured Indian youth to Cambodia under false pretenses for legitimate jobs and lucrative salaries. Victims were forced to work for scam companies, subjected to mental and physical torture, including electric shocks, forceful confinement, and denial of food and water.  The NIA is working to track down the remaining members of the syndicate.

articles.title: New banknote designs await cabinet nod - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Jameel Ahmad, State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) governor, announced that new currency note designs have been finalized and are awaiting approval from the federal cabinet.  He also addressed concerns about inflation, stating it could exceed seven percent in the last quarter of FY26 but the SBP remains committed to its medium-term target range.  Ahmad highlighted progress on licensing for virtual assets, a strong current account balance, and increased SME financing. He acknowledged global economic challenges impacting exports, but emphasized government efforts to reverse the trend.

articles.title: IMF sets Rs17.1tr federal revenue target for 2026-27 - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has projected Pakistan's federal revenues to reach Rs17.144 trillion for FY27, a significant increase of 13.5% from the current fiscal year. The IMF also expects an average inflation rate of 8.4% and economic growth at 3.5%.  Pakistan has agreed to several measures including increasing the BISP payment to Rs18,000, raising the petroleum levy target by 18%, and mobilizing additional provincial revenue through improved collection from general sales tax and agricultural income tax. The IMF is also monitoring Pakistan's efforts to address issues like circular debt flow, power sector subsidies, and corruption.  The IMF staff mission is currently in Pakistan to finalize these budgetary proposals before the budget for FY2026-27 is presented to the cabinet and parliament.

articles.title: One month of Samrat Choudhary Government in Bihar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Samrat Choudhary, the leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), took office as Chief Minister of Bihar on April 15, 2026.  He has implemented several initiatives focusing on development and combating corruption, including a blueprint for 11 satellite townships across 10 districts. The government also launched the "Police Didi Scheme" to enhance women's safety, established a three-tier public support system, and approved significant funding for education and infrastructure projects. Choudhary has also introduced measures to promote transparency in private schools and prioritize local contractors on civil projects.

articles.title: California county scam ad lawsuit adds to mounting Meta legal woes | Social Media News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Meta Platforms, the parent company of Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger, and Threads, is facing a new lawsuit from Santa Clara County, California. The county alleges that Meta knowingly profits from scam advertisements, which generated $7 billion in annual revenue, despite claiming to combat them.  The lawsuit claims that Meta's system flags suspected scammers but doesn't ban them unless they are 95% certain of fraud, allowing them to continue running ads for a premium fee. The county argues this practice targets vulnerable consumers and causes financial losses for California residents, particularly seniors.  Meta has denied the allegations, stating that it aggressively fights scams on its platforms and removed 159 million scam advertisements last year.

articles.title: Colorado governor commutes sentence of election denier Tina Peters | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jared Polis, the Colorado governor, commuted the nearly nine-year prison sentence of former Mesa County clerk Tina Peters, who was convicted of accessing voting equipment and copying it.  Peters will be released on parole on June 1st after Polis reduced her sentence from eight and a half years to about four and a half. Jena Griswold, Colorado's top election official, criticized the decision, arguing that it emboldens election denialism and threatens American democracy. The decision has drawn criticism from election officials across the country, who fear it signals an open season on elections.  Matt Crane, executive director of the Colorado Clerks Association, expressed anger and disappointment over Polis's decision.

articles.title: Mahmoud Khalil calls for deportation to be halted in light of new evidence | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mahmoud Khalil, a former Columbia University student, is calling for the termination of his deportation case due to new evidence suggesting that the Trump administration engineered the outcome.  Khalil's lawyers argue that "apparent procedural abnormalities" support their claim that the administration weaponized a farcical proceeding. The case has been flagged as high priority before reaching the Board of Immigration Appeals, and three judges recused themselves from the case, raising concerns about potential interference. Khalil maintains he was unjustly targeted for his pro-Palestine activism and has never been charged with a crime.

articles.title: Ex-Sinaloa security chief in Mexico arrested in US over alleged cartel ties | Corruption News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Gerardo Merida Sanchez, a former security chief in Mexico's Sinaloa state, was arrested in Arizona on May 11 and transferred to New York. He is accused of conspiring with leaders of the Sinaloa Cartel to import narcotics into the United States in exchange for political support and bribes.  Merida Sanchez allegedly accepted over $100,000 in monthly cash bribes from Los Chapitos, a powerful faction of the cartel led by the sons of jailed drug lord Joaquin "El Chapo" Guzman. The indictment also accuses him of leaking sensitive intelligence to the cartel. Claudia Sheinbaum, Mexico's president, has stated that she will not protect anyone who committed a crime but suggested the US charges were politically motivated.

articles.title: Super-rich NRI who called himself 'recession-proof' in 2008 sent to jail: His New Jersey mansion had salt water pool surrounded by imported sand
articles.rephrased_article: Parmjit “Paul” Parmar, an Indian-origin investor, has been sentenced to five years in prison for conspiracy to commit securities fraud. Parmar, who previously declared himself recession-proof and boasted a lavish lifestyle, was found guilty of inflating revenues, falsifying bank records, and misleading investors in a publicly traded healthcare services company where he served as CEO. The fraud is estimated to have involved over $212 million.  The scheme, orchestrated by Parmar and others including Sotirios Zaharis, a/k/a “Sam Zaharis,” and Ravi Chivukula, defrauded investors of hundreds of millions of dollars in connection with the funding of a healthcare services company's acquisition.

articles.title: CBI launches AI-powered notice verification system ‘Abhay’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has launched an AI-based helpbot called “Abhay” to authenticate CBI notices and combat cyber fraud. The agency stated that cyber-enabled fraud is a growing problem in India's criminal justice system, exacerbated by advancements in technologies like artificial intelligence.  Citizens can access Abhay through the CBI’s official website at www.cbi.gov.in.

articles.title: 50 Green Card holders identified to be deported as US starts re-vetting older cases
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Homeland Security has established a new unit, the "Tactical Operations Division," to re-vet Green Card applications. The unit, headed by Daniel Andrade, has identified at least 50 individuals through its review process and found that 80% of those cases were clean, requiring no further action.  Experts argue that this exercise is meaningless as Green Cards are already subject to extensive vetting. However, the unit can potentially lead to deportation for those convicted of crimes or who obtained their status fraudulently.

articles.title: Thousands in black robes with doubtful degrees: CJI Kant - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant criticized what he called "attacks on the judiciary" by media, social media, and RTI activists during a hearing regarding an advocate's plea for contempt proceedings over alleged delay in implementing senior advocate guidelines. The Bench, also comprising Joymalya Bagchi, dismissed the petition, stating that senior advocate designation is not a status symbol but a distinction conferred by the court.  The court expressed concern over fake law degrees and urged the CBI to investigate.

articles.title: Lawmakers decry slow internet in National Assembly, across country - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Several members of the National Assembly raised concerns about slow internet connectivity affecting the paperless working environment in parliament.  Deputy Speaker Ghulam Mustafa Shah directed authorities to address the issue, while Federal Information Technology and Telecom Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja assured them that the spectrum auction would improve internet facilities. Khawaja also addressed concerns over digital harassment, online fraud, and data theft, emphasizing public awareness campaigns and collaboration with relevant institutions.

articles.title: Indian magnate Adani agrees to multi-million-dollar penalty in US court case - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Gautam Adani, chairman of the Adani Group, agreed to pay a $18 million civil penalty in a US court case related to bribery allegations. The settlement, without admitting guilt, comes as US prosecutors are reportedly set to drop charges against Adani.  The case involved accusations that Adani and his subordinates misled investors about lucrative solar energy contracts obtained through bribes paid to Indian officials.

articles.title: Adani Enterprises, other Adani Group stocks jump up to 3%. Here’s why - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Gautam Adani and his nephew Sagar agreed to pay a combined $18 million to settle allegations of false and misleading statements made about Adani Green Energy. The proposed settlement, filed in federal court, still requires approval from a judge.  The U.S. Justice Department is also considering dropping charges against Adani, who has appointed new legal counsel including Robert J. Giuffra Jr., one of Donald Trump's personal lawyers. These developments come as the Adani Group seeks to resolve various investigations and re-enter international capital markets.

articles.title: Adani Group: Gautam Adani, nephew Sagar to pay $18m to settle civil fraud case in the US
articles.rephrased_article: Gautam Adani and his nephew, Sagar Adani, have agreed to pay $18 million to settle a civil fraud lawsuit filed by the US Securities and Exchange Commission. The 2024 lawsuit accused them of paying bribes to Indian officials for renewable energy projects and misleading US investors about anti-bribery practices.  The proposed agreement, which does not admit or deny the allegations, also bars the Adanis from future violations of key US anti-fraud laws.

articles.title: Punjab police want Anmol alias Pinky’s custody from Sindh - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Punjab Police are seeking custody of drug dealer Anmol alias Pinky from Sindh Police after her arrest in Karachi for allegedly running a drug network.  The investigation has revealed that Anmol and her brothers, Nasir and Riaz Baloch, were involved in three drug cases registered in Lahore several years ago. The Punjab Police are also investigating allegations of bribery and negligence by former officers of the Crime Investigation Agency (CIA) who allegedly avoided arresting Anmol.  The DIG investigation, Zeeshan Raza, stated that departmental action has been initiated against the officers involved.

articles.title: Compromised PM didn't sign trade deal with U.S., but a bargain for Adani's release: Rahul - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of negotiating a trade deal with the U.S. to secure the release of billionaire businessman Gautam Adani.  The U.S. government agreed to settle a lawsuit against Adani, who was accused of bribery in connection with a solar energy project. Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh criticized the deal, suggesting it was a "bargain" for **Adani's release".

articles.title: Congress leader and former Jharkhand Minister, Alamgir Alam, walks out of jail - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Alamgir Alam, a former Jharkhand minister, was released on bail from the Birsa Munda Central Jail in Ranchi after the Supreme Court granted relief in his money laundering case.  The Enforcement Directorate (ED) arrested Alam and his OSD, Sanjiv Kumar Lal, in 2024 following the seizure of nearly ₹32.20 crore from a flat linked to them. The Congress party fielded Alam's wife, Nishat Alam, as their candidate for the Pakur Assembly constituency in the 2024 elections, where she won. Babulal Marandi, the Leader of Opposition in the Jharkhand Assembly, criticized the celebration surrounding Alam's release, stating that it was premature and did not equate to an acquittal. He emphasized that the trial is ongoing and the legal process will continue until a final verdict is reached.

articles.title: BoB looks to sell Rs 2,700 crore of NPAs; taps ARCs, NBFCs - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bank of Baroda is selling a portfolio of 10 stressed accounts, totaling over ₹1,900 crore. The largest exposure is at Shirpur Power, followed by Ushdev International and Pixion Media.  The sale will be conducted on a cash basis with assets transferred "as is where is, without recourse." Bidders must be unconnected to the promoters or guarantors of the stressed accounts.

articles.title: CBI conducts searches in Reliance Communications case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) conducted searches at seven premises linked to former executives of Reliance Communications Limited (RCom) in Mumbai, Gurugram, and Bengaluru. The searches are part of ongoing investigations into alleged fraud cases involving Rs 27,337 crore reported by various Public Sector Banks and LIC. These investigations stem from the last few months when the CBI registered seven cases against the Anil Ambani-led Reliance Group.

articles.title: ED arrests Kolkata Police DC Shantanu Sinha Biswas in money laundering case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Enforcement Directorate (ED) officials arrested Shantanu Sinha Biswas, Deputy Commissioner of Kolkata Police, on Thursday for his alleged involvement in land grabbing and money laundering linked to businessman Sona Pappu.  The arrest follows repeated summons by the ED and a lookout notice issued against him for failing to appear. The investigation is ongoing, with the ED seeking information from the West Bengal Police regarding Biswas' current deployment. This marks the second high-profile arrest by the ED since the change of regime in West Bengal.

articles.title: U.S. to drop graft charges against Gautam Adani: NY Times - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: U.S. prosecutors are dropping charges against Gautam Adani, the chairman of the Adani Group, who was accused of bribing Indian officials for solar energy contracts.  The move, brought under the Biden administration, followed a meeting between Adani’s lawyers and prosecutors at the Department of Justice where Giuffra, one of President Donald Trump's personal lawyers, presented proposals for an investment in the American economy.

articles.title: Tape shows Bolsonaro son asking jailed banker for $26.8m to fund film on father | Brazil | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Flávio Bolsonaro, a leading right-wing presidential hopeful in Brazil, was caught on tape asking a convicted banker, Daniel Vorcaro, for $26.8 million to fund a film about his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro. The incident has sparked significant backlash and raised questions about the source of funds for the proposed biopic, which would feature Jim Caviezel as Jair Bolsonaro.  The scandal further complicates Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, as it highlights potential corruption within the family and raises concerns about his anti-establishment credentials.

articles.title: Trump administration pledges $1.8bn in additional humanitarian aid to UN | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration announced an additional $1.8 billion in humanitarian aid to the United Nations, bringing the total pledged to $2 billion since December. This amount falls short of past US commitments to humanitarian aid, which reached as high as $17 billion in fiscal year 2022. The Trump administration framed this smaller sum as evidence of its push for greater government efficiency and reform at the UN.  However, critics warn that the cuts could undermine human rights and global safety.

articles.title: Sri Lanka’s Fisheries Minister urges CM Vijay to ban bottom trawling - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sri Lanka’s Fisheries Minister Ramalingam Chandrasekar urged Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to ban bottom trawling fishing, a practice prohibited in Sri Lanka since 2017, as he believes it is the root cause of ongoing conflict between the two states.  Chandrasekar expressed hope for diplomatic resolution and a meeting with Vijay, congratulating him on his recent election win. He praised Vijay's letter to External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar seeking intervention in the release of six Tamil Nadu fishermen arrested by the Sri Lankan Navy for fishing illegally in Sri Lankan waters. Chandrasekar stated that arrests are made because bottom trawling destroys marine resources and threatens livelihoods, emphasizing the need for a ban on this practice in Tamil Nadu to prevent future conflicts.

articles.title: Jerome Powell: Steering the US Fed through COVID-19 and political pressures | Banks News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Jerome Powell, who served as chair of the US Federal Reserve Board of Governors from 2018 to May 15, 2023, faced political pressure from President Donald Trump throughout his tenure.  Powell's term was marked by tension between the White House and the central bank, with Trump pushing for more aggressive interest rate cuts than the Fed was willing to implement. Despite these pressures, Powell prioritized the Fed's independence and consistently defended its actions against criticism from the president. Kevin Warsh, a former member of the central bank's board of governors, will succeed Powell as chair on May 15th.  Warsh has pledged to maintain the Fed's independence and is expected to navigate the institution through continued political pressures.

articles.title: Setback for NDA as RJD wins MLC byelection in Bihar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) won the Bhojpur-Buxar Legislative Council seat in a byelection, defeating the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) candidate. Sonu Rai, representing the RJD, secured victory with 2,486 votes, while his opponent, Kanhaiya Prasad of the JD(U), received 2,146 votes. The RJD has attributed their win to alleged manipulation and fraud in the electoral process.

articles.title: US reportedly dropped fraud charges against Indian billionaire after he hired Trump’s lawyer | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Department of Justice has dropped fraud charges against Indian billionaire Gautam Adani after he hired a new legal team led by Donald Trump's personal lawyer, Robert J Giuffra Jr.  Giuffra presented a plan for Adani to invest $10 billion in the US economy and create 15,000 jobs if the charges were dropped. Prosecutors stated that the potential investment wouldn't sway their decision, but one official found it favorable. Adani was accused of bribing Indian officials and misleading investors with false statements.

articles.title: Indian-origin doctor under probe for 'birth tourism' in San Jose: 'Foreign expectant mothers get extra service'
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Athiya Javid, a physician from San Jose, is under investigation by the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform for allegedly promoting birth tourism through her website and affiliated entities.  The committee sent letters to Dr. Javid, Doctores Para Ti, Have My Baby in Miami, and International Maternity Services, requesting documents related to their alleged involvement in birth tourism. The investigation stems from concerns about potential national security and election integrity threats posed by foreign nationals traveling for the purpose of giving birth in the United States, particularly those from China and Russia.

articles.title: CBI arrests key accused in cyber fraud case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested Lakhan Jaiprakash Jagwani, a key suspect in a transnational cyber-enabled financial fraud case involving illegal call centers targeting U.S. nationals. The syndicate operated since 2022 and impersonated officials from agencies like the DEA, FBI, and Social Security Administration to defraud victims of $8.5 million.  The agency previously seized ₹1.88 crore in cash from an "illegal" call center run by Jagwani in Noida.

articles.title: Palestinian President Abbas pledges elections, reform at Fatah conference | Fatah News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mahmoud Abbas, the Palestinian Authority president, was unanimously re-elected leader of the Fatah movement at a party conference in Ramallah. Abbas pledged to reform the PA and hold long-delayed presidential and parliamentary elections.  He also emphasized the need for "solutions, not slogans" as the Palestinian national movement faces significant challenges. The conference comes amid mounting pressure from international actors for reforms and elections, with key figures like Jibril Rajoub and Hussein al-Sheikh vying to replace Abbas in the post-Abbas era.

articles.title: ‘It’s like stealing’: Palestinian family’s seized property listed on Booking.com | West Bank | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A new report by Ekō, a US-based advocacy group, has revealed that 41 Booking.com listings in 14 illegal Israeli settlements across the occupied West Bank are being advertised on the global travel site. The report argues that these bookings constitute money laundering and violate international law.  Booking.com, headquartered in the Netherlands, is under scrutiny for its role in this situation as it faces a criminal complaint alleging its involvement in supporting illegal settlements. Airbnb, another major accommodation platform, has also been criticized for listing properties in these settlements despite previously vowing to stop advertising them.

articles.title: Civil servants’ asset declarations to be made public in redacted form, says govt - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The government announced that asset declarations of civil servants will be made publicly accessible in a redacted form to ensure transparency while safeguarding personal privacy. Establishment Division Secretary Nabeel Awan testified before the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue, stating that the revised Civil Servants Conduct Rules are being implemented and the system is being digitized through the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) platform.  The committee also discussed missing silver from Customs custody, an investigation into the matter was initiated by the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA), and a report on recovery and identification of those involved was requested. The committee deferred the discussion on proposed amendments to the Pakistan Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 due to concerns over potential impact on state-owned enterprises (SOEs).

articles.title: 3 things OPT employers should check as ICE announces crackdown on 10,000 foreign students
articles.rephrased_article: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) announced a crackdown on foreign students participating in the Optional Practical Training program, uncovering widespread fraud involving fake companies and non-existent work sites. Emily Neumann, an immigration attorney, advises companies to verify their Form I-983s, ensure supervisors are aware of training responsibilities, and report terminations within five business days. ICE found empty buildings, residential addresses listed as work sites, coordinated employer clusters, and a single owner operating multiple entities to evade taxes and obscure employment relationships.

articles.title: Indian-origin former CEO sentenced to 5 years in prison over $212 million fraud in New Jersey, asked to pay $125 million
articles.rephrased_article: Parmjit Parmar, a 55-year-old Indian-origin man from New Jersey, was sentenced to five years in prison for his involvement in a large-scale securities fraud scheme. Parmar, also known as Paul Parmer, pleaded guilty in 2025 and orchestrated the scheme with co-conspirators Sotirios Zaharis (aka 'Sam Zaharis') and Ravi Chivukula. The conspirators defrauded a private investment firm and others out of hundreds of millions of dollars by inflating the value of a healthcare services company.  The scheme involved falsifying bank records, creating phony customers, and misrepresenting financial information to raise money for acquisitions that did not exist.

articles.title: Indian-origin former CEO sentenced to 5 years in prison over $212 million fraud in New Jersey, asked to pay $125 million
articles.rephrased_article: Parmjit Parmar, a 55-year-old Indian-origin man from New Jersey, was sentenced to five years in prison for his role in a large-scale investment fraud scheme. Parmar, along with co-conspirators Sotirios Zaharis and Ravi Chivukula, defrauded investors by inflating the value of a healthcare services company and securing funding through fraudulent means. The conspirators misrepresented the company's financial performance, causing victims to believe it was worth significantly more than its actual value.  The scheme ultimately led to the company's bankruptcy in 2018.

articles.title: Iraq’s parliament approves new Ali al-Zaidi government | Government News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iraq’s parliament approved a partial cabinet for Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, who was sworn in despite failing to secure consensus on key positions, including interior and defense.  Al-Zaidi's government includes 14 ministers, but the lineup remains incomplete as negotiations continue between political parties. The new prime minister faces challenges such as disarming Iran-backed militias and balancing ties between Washington and Tehran. Al-Zaidi was chosen to form the government after President Nizar Amedi named him prime minister-designate and tasked him with forming a government.

articles.title: 'You are doing nonsense': Indian man counters Texas whistleblower Sara Gonzales over H-1B allegation, calls her jobless
articles.rephrased_article: Sara Gonzales, a Texas journalist, targeted Great America Technologies for alleged H-1B fraud in her latest video.  The confrontation between Gonzales and the company's director, Nagarjuna Reddy Sakam, escalated into an altercation with Sakam claiming his business is legitimate and not engaging in illegal activities.  Sakam threatened legal action against Gonzales for what he perceived as harassment and trespassing.  James Blunt, a US entrepreneur who frequently comments on immigration issues, reviewed the company's operations and found no wrongdoing.

articles.title: Canadian officer accused of spying for China acquitted of charges | Canada | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: William Majcher, a retired RCMP officer, was acquitted of national security charges after a British Columbia supreme court justice found the Crown failed to prove he acted illegally. The case involved allegations that Majcher helped Chinese police coerce a Vancouver-area real estate investor back to China.  The judge deemed the prosecution's evidence "entirely circumstantial" and questioned the basis for the RCMP's arrest, suggesting it was driven by "a hunch or generalized suspicion."

articles.title: Saleh Mamman: Former Nigerian power minister sentenced to 75 years for corruption
articles.rephrased_article: Saleh Mamman, a former Nigerian power minister, was sentenced to 75 years in prison for laundering $24.7 million in public funds. Mamman, who led the ministry under President Muhammadu Buhari from 2015 to 2021, was found guilty of 12 counts related to using private firms to funnel money linked to government-funded power plants.  The case is part of a wider anti-corruption drive targeting former government officials in Nigeria. The high court ordered Mamman to repay $16 million and his conviction has reignited public anger over the country's chronic electricity crisis.

articles.title: Modern antisemitism built on old Jewish stereotypes and tropes, royal commission told | Royal commission on antisemitism and social cohesion | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Dr Dave Rich, the Community Security Trust’s policy director, testified before the royal commission into antisemitism and social cohesion that modern-day antisemitism has evolved from traditional tropes found in documents like the Protocols of the Elders of Zion. Rich explained that these negative stereotypes about Jewish people, often rooted in historical accusations such as blood libel or claims of being Christ killers, persist today and are frequently used to justify violence against Jews. He emphasized the need for governments to define antisemitism to combat it effectively while acknowledging the complexities of determining when criticism of Israel crosses into antisemitic territory.

articles.title: Rescuers search rubble of Kyiv flats after massive Russian strikes kill two
articles.rephrased_article: Russia launched a massive wave of strikes against Ukraine, killing two and injuring 40 in Kyiv, where rescuers are searching through the rubble of a nine-storey apartment block.  The attack followed a major assault on Wednesday, marking the third consecutive day of Ukrainian deaths as Moscow ramps up its offensive after a three-day ceasefire expired. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged allies to pressure Russia, while Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko called for strengthened air defense.  The attacks also targeted other regions including Kremenchuk, Bila Tserkva, Kharkiv, Sumy, and Odesa.  Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha condemned the attack as "barbaric" and urged US President Donald Trump and China's Xi Jinping to exert pressure on Putin.

articles.title: J D Vance: 'Home Alone' at White House: Vance jokes as Trump visits China for key talks - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Vice President J D Vance compared his current situation at the White House to Macaulay Culkin in "Home Alone" due to US Secret Service protocols that prevent him from traveling abroad with President Donald Trump.  Vance, who leads the Anti-Fraud Taskforce, warned of potential federal funding cuts for state health insurance programs if states do not cooperate with the Trump administration's crackdown on fraud. President Trump is currently in China and expected to return this Saturday.

articles.title: NEET-UG, 2026 paper leak: Experts call for reforms in exam process, exemption of State-government seats - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Doctors’ Association for Social Equality (DASE) general secretary G.R. Ravindranath and Indian Medical Association (IMA) former president Rajeev Jayadevan have called for compulsory registration of all medical entrance exam coaching centers, a computerised NEET exam, and exemption of state-government controlled medical seats from the single-window national system to prevent malpractices in the exam.  They also suggested free coaching centers with boarding facilities for poor students and the use of technology like encrypted questions and multi-session testing to ensure a fair and merit-based process.

articles.title: NSUI holds protest outside Education Minister’s residence over NEET paper leak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Members of the National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) protested outside Dharmendra Pradhan's residence in Delhi, demanding his resignation following allegations of a paper leak in the NEET-UG 2026 examination. The protesters accused the Education Minister of failing to protect students and demanded a Supreme Court-monitored investigation into the incident, along with action against those involved. The National Testing Agency (NTA) cancelled the exam and announced it would be retaken at a later date.

articles.title: JD Vance threatens health funding to states that don’t comply with White House anti-fraud effort | US healthcare | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: JD Vance, the US vice-president, threatened to withhold federal funding for government health insurance programs in states that fail to comply with a crackdown on suspected fraud. CMS, the agency responsible for Medicaid and Medicare, announced a six-month halt on new Medicare enrollment for hospices and home health agencies while investigating potential fraud alongside Vance's taskforce.  The administration will review anti-fraud funding for states deemed non-compliant, but it is unclear how extensive these actions will be or what impact they will have on access to care.

articles.title: Israel’s ruling coalition proposes early elections amid ultra-Orthodox anger at Netanyahu | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli prime minister, has proposed dissolving parliament to trigger early elections. The move comes after mounting pressure from ultra-Orthodox parties and follows a possible collapse of his coalition.  The bill, signed by leaders of the governing coalition, could be put to a vote on May 20th. Yair Lapid, leader of the opposition, has responded with his own proposal to dissolve parliament. The upcoming elections are expected to take place in August, potentially two months before the original end of the legislative term.

articles.title: Kevin Warsh confirmed as new US Federal Reserve chair amid controversy | Banks News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh as the new chair of the Federal Reserve’s Board of Governors, succeeding Jerome Powell, in a 54-45 vote.  Warsh's confirmation comes amid concerns about independence at the central bank and rising inflation. He was previously on the board from 2006 to 2011 and has advocated for rate cuts under Donald Trump. Warsh’s swearing-in awaits final White House signatures.

articles.title: OPT faces fresh political heat in US amid fraud allegations; Intl students will face the brunt - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Acting Director Todd Lyons announced the identification of over 10,000 foreign students linked to “highly suspect employers” in a crackdown on fraud within the Optional Practical Training (OPT) program.  Lyons described the OPT program as a "magnet for fraud" and warned of potential criminal, civil, and immigration consequences. Immigration lawyers and education experts have long cautioned against fraudulent consultancies and fake staffing arrangements within the OPT ecosystem, but this latest crackdown is expected to fuel ongoing political efforts by conservative groups to scale back or eliminate the program.  The recent briefing has caused anxiety among international students, particularly Indian students, who are the largest cohort in the OPT program.

articles.title: West Bengal CM gives sanction to CBI to prosecute officials in several scams - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari, West Bengal Chief Minister, granted permission to the CBI to prosecute officials involved in teacher's recruitment, municipality recruitment, and cooperative scams.  He stated that these investigations were previously withheld by the previous Trinamool Congress government due to corruption concerns. The move is part of a "zero tolerance" policy against corruption adopted by his BJP-led administration.  The Chief Minister also lifted a ban on potato sales to other states, citing a bumper crop and falling prices.

articles.title: ATS questions 57 in Maharashtra over alleged gangster network links - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) officials conducted searches across several cities in the state as part of an operation targeting alleged networks linked to Pakistani gangsters, including the Shahzad Bhatti gang and the Dogra gang. The focus is on identifying sleeper cells, local operatives, and support systems that may facilitate arms smuggling or conspiracies.  ATS teams seized electronic devices and are examining bank accounts and financial transactions to determine if funds were routed from Pakistan through hawala channels.

articles.title: Australia politics live: Albanese denies tax reforms aimed at courting votes from growing gen Z cohort | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Anthony Albanese denied that the additional 700,000 gen Z voters being added to the electoral roll by the time of the next federal election influenced the negative gearing and capital gains tax changes in Tuesday's budget. Albanese stated his focus was on good policy for young Australians and social cohesion, arguing the government could not "sit back and continue to watch" income from labor treated differently than income from assets. Taylor, the opposition leader, pledged to fight against the budget legislation and argued it would hurt aspirational Aussies.

articles.title: Cartel corruption claims push US-Mexico relations to breaking point | Mexico | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tensions between Mexico and the United States are at a breaking point, fueled by accusations of collaboration between Mexican officials and drug traffickers. Claudia Sheinbaum, Mexico's current mayor, has denied these allegations while facing pressure from Washington to address cartel activity.  The situation is further complicated by reports of CIA involvement in operations against cartels, including the alleged assassination of a mid-level cartel member. Despite denials, Sheinbaum faces mounting pressure to hand over officials accused of ties to drug trafficking organizations, potentially jeopardizing her relationship with the US.

articles.title: Russia targets Ukraine with more than 800 drones in deadly daytime assault | Ukraine | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Russia launched a large-scale drone attack on Ukraine, targeting critical infrastructure and killing at least six people. The attacks came hours after a previous barrage, escalating tensions between the two countries despite recent claims by Donald Trump that the war could end soon.  Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Ukraine's president, condemned the attacks while Hungary's foreign minister called for action against attacks on ethnic Hungarian regions. Meanwhile, Slovakia closed its border crossings with Ukraine due to security concerns.

articles.title: IHC rules high courts can assume jurisdiction in cases of promotion assessments - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Islamabad High Court ruled that high courts can review decisions made by the Central Selection Board (CSB) regarding promotions for top bureaucrats. The court overturned the CSB's supersession and deferment of several officers, including those from the Police Service of Pakistan, Pakistan Administrative Service, Inland Revenue Service, Pakistan Customs Service, and health sector.  The court found that the CSB’s decision-making process lacked fairness and transparency, citing procedural impropriety in communication of reasons for decisions. The judgment emphasized constitutional guarantees of fairness and due process, directing the Federation to reconsider promotions based on merit and fitness.

articles.title: Mityana dog scam: Dozens of dogs rescued and suspect arrested in Uganda after BBC investigation
articles.rephrased_article: Police and animal rights organizations in Uganda rescued dozens of dogs from sham shelters after a BBC investigation exposed online scams. Owen Godfrey Membe, who was arrested, is accused of animal cruelty. The Animal Welfare Alliance Uganda, a network of local and international activists, has secured land for an emergency shelter to care for the rescued dogs.  The case against Membe was brought as a private prosecution by the Animal Justice Center with funding from We Won't Be Scammed.

articles.title: Court overturns Alex Murdaugh's murder convictions
articles.rephrased_article: The South Carolina Supreme Court overturned the 2023 murder convictions of Alex Murdaugh, a disgraced lawyer convicted of killing his wife and son. The court ruled that Colleton County Clerk of Court Rebecca Hill unfairly biased the jury against Murdaugh by making comments to jurors during the trial.  Hill has since pleaded guilty to charges related to misconduct in office and obstruction of justice. The justices cited numerous comments made by Hill to jurors, including her telling them not to trust Murdaugh's testimony and urging them to speed up the verdict.

articles.title: Why Trump decided to back Iraq’s prime minister-designate, Ali al-Zaidi | US-Israel war on Iran | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump publicly supported Ali al-Zaidi, a pro-Iran Iraqi politician, as the country's next prime minister after pressure from Washington to avoid an Iran-aligned government.  The US suspended aid and security assistance to Iraq in order to prevent the nomination of former Prime Minister Nouri al-Maliki, who was backed by the Coordination Framework, a Shia party coalition aligned with Iran. The US Secretary of Treasury, Scott Bessent, warned that those enabling militia violence would be held accountable. Al-Zaidi's appointment is conditional on progress in curbing pro-Iran militia activity and removing them from Iraqi institutions.

articles.title: NIA arrests Hizb-ul-Mujahideen linked ‘narco-terrorist’ after extradition from Portugal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) arrested Iqbal Singh, also known as Shera, in Delhi after securing his extradition from Portugal. Singh, a mastermind in a major Hizb-ul-Mujahideen (HM) terror-financing case, had fled to Portugal in 2020 and was wanted for a non-bailable arrest warrant issued in October 2020 and an Interpol Red Notice opened in June 2021. The NIA alleges that Singh coordinated the smuggling of heroin from Pakistan into India and channeled proceeds through "hawala" networks to HM operatives in Pakistan and Kashmir, facilitating terror activities.

articles.title: 1MDB financier Jho Low seeks pardon from Donald Trump | 1MDB | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jho Low, a fugitive Malaysian financier, has reportedly requested a pardon from President Donald Trump.  Low faces multiple charges in the US and Malaysia related to his alleged role in the misappropriation of at least $4.5 billion from 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB). The scandal is one of the world’s biggest financial frauds, with billions plundered from the now defunct sovereign wealth fund. Johari Abdul Ghani, chair of a Malaysian taskforce seeking to recover funds and assets linked to 1MDB, opposes Low's request for a pardon and urges the US to assist Malaysia in locating him.

articles.title: Tens of thousands protest in Argentina over Milei university cuts | Protests News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Tens of thousands of Argentines protested in cities across the country against Javier Milei's government's cuts to public university funding. The demonstrations, fueled by concerns over staff wages and a stalled funding law, highlight growing discontent with Milei's policies, which have led to declining real salaries for professors and accusations of corruption within his administration.  The protesters argue that the cuts undermine the foundations of higher education in Argentina, a country known for its public universities' history of producing Nobel laureates.

articles.title: ‘Blatant disregard for rights’: concern grows over Gabon’s social media clampdown | Gabon | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Gabon’s government indefinitely suspended major social media platforms in February, citing security concerns and the spread of misinformation.  This action led to a surge in VPN usage but also resulted in arrests and account suspensions for activists and opposition members. Nelly Ngabima, a controversial activist, reported threats from government officials who accused her of identity theft. Rights groups have condemned the restrictions as a violation of freedom of expression. Despite temporary lifting of the ban in April, new regulations mandate verified information from social media users or face fines and imprisonment.  The crackdown on dissent has been criticized by opposition figures and human rights organizations.

articles.title: Supreme Court to hear ED plea against bail granted to accused in West Bengal coal scam case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court agreed to hear the Enforcement Directorate’s (ED) appeal against the grant of anticipatory bail to Anup Majee, accused of leading a coal mining scam in West Bengal. The ED claims that Mr. Majee operated with the “active” assistance of several leaders from the All India Trinamool Congress.  The court sought Mr. Majee’s response to the agency's plea challenging a June 2025 order granting him bail in a money laundering case registered in 2020.

articles.title: BJP targets DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin over Sanatana Dharma remarks - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) condemned Udhayanidhi Stalin, a DMK leader, for his remarks on Sanatana Dharma in the Tamil Nadu Assembly.  G. Kishan Reddy, Union Minister for Coal and Mines, accused the DMK of "poisonous politics" and "anti-Hindu rhetoric." The BJP also criticized the Congress party's support for Stalin's comments and questioned Vijay, the newly elected Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, on his silence regarding the issue.

articles.title: Honduras mayor arrested for masterminding environmentalist’s killing | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Honduran authorities arrested Adan Funez, former mayor of Tocoa, for allegedly orchestrating the 2024 assassination of environmental activist Juan Lopez.  F Nunez was captured at his home on Tuesday and joins two other suspects, businessman Hector Eduardo Méndez and Juan Angel Ramos Gallegos, who are accused of criminal association to the detriment of fundamental rights. The arrests follow years of accusations against Funez by religious and environmental leaders and come after a string of prior arrests related to Lopez's death.  The trial is set for next June.

articles.title: Major ICE crackdown on 10,000 foreign students on OPT; 'fake companies' being operated from India - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: ICE director Todd M Lyons announced a crackdown on the Optional Practical Training (OPT) program, citing fraud and irregularities involving nearly 10,000 foreign students.  Lyons stated that the program's size has ballooned since its creation under the Bush administration, with hundreds of thousands of students working in the US instead of the anticipated few thousand. ICE investigators have uncovered suspicious employers, including empty buildings, locked doors, and financial red flags like breaches of contract and suspicious cash movement across countries. The findings suggest a coordinated employer network where multiple OPT workers are employed at nearly identical websites.

articles.title: NEET-UG examination 2026: One suspect arrested from Nashik - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Testing Agency (NTA) cancelled the NEET-UG examination for 2026 after an alleged paper leak, leading to the arrest of a suspect in Maharashtra. The Rajasthan Police requested the Maharashtra police to detain the individual who was apprehended after changing his appearance.  The cancellation has drawn criticism from opposition leaders, including Rohit Pawar, who pointed out that the state government's new law against paper leaks is insufficient and called for stricter action against those involved. A CBI inquiry into the matter has been initiated.

articles.title: H-1B scam: Texas company owned by Chinese national sued for selling foreign workers visas for $20,000 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has filed a lawsuit against Golden Qi Holdings LLC, a Texas company owned by a Chinese national, Yuan Yao. The lawsuit alleges that the company ran fake childcare businesses to fraudulently obtain H-1B visas for foreign workers.  The case cites examples of non-existent facilities and claims that the companies received federal loans intended for childcare operations but were not used for those purposes.  Paxton stated his office will continue to investigate suspected H-1B visa fraud in North Texas, where authorities say some companies may be running "ghost" operations while sponsoring foreign workers.

articles.title: Israel’s war creating a ‘lost generation’ of Lebanese students | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel’s war on Lebanon has displaced hundreds of thousands of students and teachers, creating a “lost generation” and widening societal disparities. Schools have been destroyed or turned into shelters, disrupting education and causing further disruptions to an already struggling system.  While some institutions are using online learning, experts say this is ineffective for many vulnerable students due to limited access to technology and resources. The war has exacerbated Lebanon's economic crisis and humanitarian challenges, leading to increased poverty and forcing families to make difficult choices between basic needs like food and education. Experts warn that without significant intervention, these disparities could have long-term consequences for the country’s future.

articles.title: Zelensky's ex-chief of staff in court as Ukraine corruption probe escalates
articles.rephrased_article: Andriy Yermak, former chief of staff to President Volodymyr Zelensky, appeared in a Kyiv court on Tuesday as part of an ongoing corruption probe.  The Anticorruption Prosecutor's Office (Sapo) and the National anti-corruption bureau (Nabu) are investigating allegations of money laundering surrounding a luxury construction project outside Kyiv. Yermak, who was close to Zelensky until his resignation last year following an anti-corruption raid on his flat, denies wrongdoing. The investigation has cast a shadow over Ukraine's bid for EU membership and comes as Russia marks victory over Nazi Germany in World War Two with renewed attacks on Ukraine.

articles.title: Indian engineer charged in US for Maryland bridge crash, six construction workers were killed in 2024 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Synergy Marine Pte Ltd, based in Singapore, and Synergy Maritime Pte Ltd, based in Chennai, India, along with Indian engineer Radhakrishnan Karthik Nair, have been charged by the US Department of Justice for conspiring to defraud the country and causing the death of six construction workers in a 2024 bridge crash. The companies are accused of failing to inform authorities about a hazardous condition, obstructing an agency proceeding, and making false statements.  The Department of Justice also alleges that the companies violated environmental laws by discharging pollutants into the Patapsco River and Chesapeake Bay.

articles.title: NSUI protests after NTA cancels NEET-UG 2026 over paper leak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A massive protest organized by the National Students' Union of India (NSUI) erupted outside the Shastri Bhawan on Tuesday, May 12, 2026, demanding justice for students alleging a paper leak in the NEET-UG exam.  The protest saw members of the Congress party's student wing participate, holding signs and slogans criticizing the government's handling of the situation. The National Testing Agency (NTA) canceled the examination following investigations by the Rajasthan Special Operations Group (SOG) and the CBI.  The NSUI accused the central government of failing to protect students and demanded the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and a ban on the NTA.

articles.title: It’s parliament, not Love Island: Queensland’s ministerial affair drama becomes a sordid distraction | Queensland politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jarrod Bleijie, the deputy premier of Queensland, during question time in parliament, revealed personal relationships of several Labor MPs and threatened to expose further information. This followed repeated questions about the relationship between two Liberal National party ministers, Tim Mander and Amanda Camm, which have been a source of controversy.  Bleijie's actions were criticized for being politically motivated and lacking substance, while some argue that both parties are failing to hold each other accountable for their policies. The incident highlights the low public interest in parliamentary proceedings and suggests that voters may be more interested in reality television than politics.

articles.title: Bolivia issues warrant for Evo Morales’s arrest after court no-show | Evo Morales News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Evo Morales, Bolivia's former president, is facing arrest after failing to appear for his trial on charges of trafficking a minor. A Bolivian judge found him in contempt of court and reissued an arrest warrant following his absence from the start of the proceedings.  Morales has denied the accusations against him and claims he will resist any attempt to capture him, with supporters vowing to fight back against authorities.

articles.title: 'Crazy': US denies OPT extension citing police record; applicant called police after being assaulted - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has denied a STEM OPT extension to an applicant based on a "law enforcement interaction," citing the individual's call to police after being assaulted. Scott Decker, an immigration attorney, argues that this decision is arbitrary and potentially discriminatory, as it unfairly penalizes individuals who have been victims of crime.  Decker believes this situation may be indicative of broader USCIS practices where they are denying benefits based on seemingly minor interactions with law enforcement without proper review.

articles.title: Royal Opera House calls for release of Georgian bass singer jailed over democracy protests | Royal Opera House | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Royal Opera House in London has urged Keir Starmer, the British Prime Minister, to intervene in the case of Paata Burchuladze, a renowned Georgian bass singer imprisoned in Georgia since October. The 71-year-old, who performed at the Royal Opera House and the Metropolitan Opera House, was sentenced to seven years in prison for alleged involvement in a coup against the country's authoritarian leader. Peter Katona, director of casting at the Royal Opera and Burchuladze’s friend, claims the charges are fabricated and that he is being persecuted for his opposition to the ruling regime.  The Foreign Office is monitoring developments closely and will raise concerns about detainees' rights.

articles.title: US Stock Market Today | Dow Jones | Nasdaq Live: S&P 500 inches to higher close, AI fervor edges out Iran impasse - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Meta Platforms Inc. is facing a lawsuit from Santa Clara County, alleging the company profits from billions of scam advertisements on its platforms.  Microsoft Corp. plans to return $92 billion from its investment in OpenAI. Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser predicts oil market stabilization could be delayed until 2027 due to disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Investors are awaiting key inflation data and consumer demand trends this week, while US Treasury yields rose on concerns over inflation and potential rate hikes.  The Clarity Act, aiming for a regulatory framework for cryptocurrencies, is expected to face opposition from both sides of the aisle.

articles.title: LHC accepts Maryam's plea seeking return of bail surety in Chaudhry Sugar Mills case - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Lahore High Court (LHC) granted an application by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, allowing the return of Rs70 million surety deposited for her bail in the Chaudhry Sugar Mills case. The National Accountability Bureau (NAB) withdrew its plea challenging directives for the closure of the investigation against Maryam, and the LHC bench accepted her request.  The court's decision follows an accountability court's March ruling allowing Maryam to withdraw her surety bond after a February 4 directive from the LHC to place a termination report before the accountability court for the closure of the investigation.

articles.title: Poland says it expects US to extradite ex-minister who fled from Hungary | Poland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Poland's foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, stated that the country expects the United States to extradite former justice minister Zbigniew Ziobro, who fled Hungary and entered the US.  Ziobro is wanted by Polish prosecutors for charges of abuse of power and corruption. The Polish government has accused him of leading a criminal group that diverted funds from victims of violence, while he denies the allegations. Ziobro claims to have entered the US using asylum documents provided by Hungary, but his presence in the country has raised questions about potential US involvement in his case.

articles.title: South Africa plans presidential impeachment probe over ‘Farmgate’ scandal | Corruption News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: South Africa's parliament will establish an impeachment committee to investigate allegations against President Cyril Ramaphosa in the "Farmgate" scandal. The move follows a decision by the country's highest court to revive impeachment proceedings, which center on the theft of $4 million in foreign currency from Ramaphosa's Phala Phala game farm.  The committee will review evidence and decide whether to recommend formal impeachment proceedings.

articles.title: Modi’s austerity drive is an admission of failure on economic and foreign policy fronts, alleges Akhilesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Akhilesh Yadav, president of the Samajwadi Party, criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi's appeal for austerity in light of the Iran conflict, accusing the BJP government of failing on both economic and foreign policy fronts.  Yadav argued that the appeal was an admission of failure and that the restrictions imposed were disproportionate to the perceived crisis. He also accused the BJP of fueling political unrest with electoral fraud and social discord.

articles.title: Philippine presidential hopeful Sara Duterte impeached for second time | Philippines | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sara Duterte, the Philippine vice-president, was impeached by an overwhelming majority of lawmakers in the House of Representatives. The accusations against her include misuse of public funds, unexplained wealth accumulation, and threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his wife, Louise Araneta-Marcos.  Duterte has denied all wrongdoing and will now face a trial in the Senate. If found guilty, she could be banned from public office, jeopardizing her presidential ambitions for 2028. The case is further complicated by Duterte's family ties to former president Rodrigo Duterte, who faces charges of crimes against humanity at the International Criminal Court.

articles.title: Philippine House Impeaches VP Sara Duterte Amid Graft Allegations | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Philippine House of Representatives voted overwhelmingly to impeach Vice President Sara Duterte, sending the impeachment complaints to the Senate for trial. The vote, with 255-26 in favor and nine abstentions, followed allegations of graft, corruption, misuse of state funds, and an alleged assassination threat against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.  The Senate elected Senator Alan Peter Cayetano as its new president shortly before the vote, a development that could influence the impeachment trial's outcome. A guilty verdict would remove Duterte from office and bar her from holding any government position for life.
